description: SimMobility is an integrated, multi-scale agent-based mobility simulation platform that links long-term (land use and housing), mid-term (daily activity and travel demand with supply) and short-term (microscopic traffic) simulators to predict how mobility demand affects transport networks, intelligent transport services and vehicle emissions under alternative technology, policy and investment scenarios. It models millions of agents, including pedestrians, drivers, cars, buses, trains and traffic lights, from second-by-second to year-by-year; a freight extension, SimMobility Freight, simulates urban goods movement and was described by Sakai and colleagues in Transportation Research Part E (2020). It is developed by the Intelligent Transportation Systems Lab at MIT and the Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology, with Singapore as its main city application. The C++ code and wiki are free on GitHub under the SimMobility Version Control Licence, which allows non-commercial use only. Caveats: there are no releases, the public repository's last commit was in March 2022, the build is complex, and calibrated city inputs are not bundled. SimMobility supports agent-based network flow and capacity planning studies of urban transport and freight under policy and investment scenarios, alongside other agent-based frameworks such as MATSim catalogued here.
